extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, organizations, and other stakeholders submitting comments to EPA dockets (Regulations.gov)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for preparing and submitting public comments to EPA rulemakings and dockets, including what to include in submissions, restrictions, data fields collected, mass-mail handling, and how EPA may process comments (including AI use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify docket ID and other identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the docket ID number and other identifying information (e.g., subject heading, Federal Register date and page number) in your subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments cannot be considered if they are misdirected or get lost because the identifying information was not included. If your comment is about a particular proposed regulatory provision, include the reference to the proposed part and section number for the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and understand the document; seek clarification if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and understand the document you are commenting on and, if you have difficulty understanding it, reach out to the EPA contact person named in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you contacted EPA for clarification, describe that difficulty in your comments along with the clarification you received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow directions provided in the document
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow directions provided by the Agency about how to respond, including responding to specific questions, providing particular information, or organizing comments in a specified way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments as requested to facilitate processing once received by EPA; failure to follow instructions may impede consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise but support your claims; be civil
rubrics_metrics.description: Be concise while supporting claims: explain views clearly, avoid profanity or personal threats, and provide reasons for agreement or disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest alternatives and substitute language for requested changes. Provide specific examples to illustrate concerns and keep language professional and non-threatening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base comments on sound reasoning, evidence, and described impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Base comments on sound reasoning, scientific evidence, and/or explanation of how you will be impacted by the agency’s proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any assumptions and provide the technical information and/or data used. If you estimate potential costs or burdens, explain how you arrived at your estimate in sufficient detail to allow for reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address trade-offs and opposing views
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss trade-offs and opposing views in your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging alternatives and counterarguments strengthens the usefulness of a comment for agency decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality over quantity (not a vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment process is not a vote—one well-supported comment is often more informative to the agency than a thousand form letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on substantive content rather than mass submissions of undifferentiated form letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit by the comment period deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure to submit your comments by the comment period deadline identified in the Federal Register document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late comments may not be considered; verify deadlines in the notice you are commenting on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threatening language or profanity will be rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments containing threatening language or profanity will be rejected without notice from the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional, non-threatening language; profanity or threats risk outright rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia submissions require a written comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make; do not rely solely on multimedia files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on content hosted outside the primary submission
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all substantive content within the primary submission on Regulations.gov or in the submitted attachment so EPA staff can review it directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyrighted material must include proof of redistribution rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of any copyrighted material without accompanying proof of one's explicit right to redistribute that material will result in the comment being blocked from online viewing at Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you incorporate copyrighted content, provide documentation proving you have the right to redistribute it; otherwise the content may be withheld from public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Confidential Business Information (CBI) and statutorily restricted information
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute should not be sent electronically via Regulations.gov or e-mail; follow EPA procedures for CBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to include CBI, clearly mark which part is claimed as CBI and also submit a non-CBI copy for the public docket. CBI will not be disclosed except as provided by 40 CFR Part 2 and/or 40 CFR Part 703 as appropriate. TSCA CBI claims have additional special requirements and must be submitted electronically using appropriate EPA tools (e.g., CDX/TSCA General Communications Tool) and include substantiation. For other statutorily restricted information, clearly mark submissions so the EPA Docket Center processes them under the applicable statute; contact EPA Docket Center for guidance if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark information claimed as statutorily restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: If you include other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute in your comment, clearly mark your submission as including that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information so marked will be processed by the EPA Docket Center in accordance with the applicable statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass mail campaign and bundled submissions posting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has special posting guidelines for mass mail campaigns and bundled submissions that affect how comments are posted to Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When individual submissions are duplicate or near duplicate as part of a mass mail campaign, EPA will post one representative sample comment along with the total comment count for that campaign. In instances where submissions are bundled together (submitted as a single document or packaged together), EPA will post all comments along with the total comment count for that campaign (this includes hardcopy-handwritten bundled campaigns scanned into PDFs). Exception: bundled campaigns of hardcopy form letters and form postcards—EPA will post one representative sample comment along with the total comment count. (Refer to the posting overview table on the page for distinctions by submission type: web/email/hardcopy.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Regulations.gov Beta comment form data fields (as of Feb 19, 2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations.gov standardized the comment form fields (Beta form) for all agencies as of Feb 19, 2021; specific fields are required or optional depending on commenter type (Individual/Organization/Anonymous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key fields on the Beta form: Comment (Required for Individual/Organization/Anonymous), Email Address (Optional), First Name (Required for Individual; N/A for Organization/Anonymous), Last Name (Required for Individual; N/A for Organization/Anonymous), City/State/Zip/Country/Phone/Attach Files/Organization Type/Organization Name/reCAPTCHA varied by commenter type as listed in the table. Prior to June 4, 2019, agencies could select which fields to provide (Classic form); between June 4, 2019 and Feb 18, 2021 both Classic and Beta were available. EPA-specific Classic form field availability is listed on the page—consult the table for exact required/optional fields depending on form version.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA posts comments publicly with specified exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted to EPA, including any personal information in the body of the submission, will be posted to Regulations.gov and are also available for in-person viewing at the EPA Docket Center’s Reading Room, subject to the exceptions noted in the Rules and Restrictions section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that personal information included in comment text may be made public unless covered by an exception (e.g., properly marked and handled CBI).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get documentation for Regulations.gov data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations.gov makes public comment data available via web interface, bulk download, and API; requests for documentation about which comment form data fields collected by EPA are made available to data users should be directed to GSA/Regulations.gov support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact regulationshelpdesk@gsa.gov or use Regulations.gov Support for documentation on data field availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA may use AI to assist with comment processing but humans remain responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may use artificial intelligence to help sort and categorize public comments for certain rulemakings and other actions, but human supervision and input are required throughout comment processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may be used to identify substantive comments, separate topical arguments, sort key points by theme, and generate individual comment summaries to aid processing. However, the basis for the agency’s response remains the underlying comments and responses to comments are drafted by humans; quality assurance processes are in place to ensure comprehensive human review.
